newsitem.title: UK: DHL Albania - it's business as usual.
newsitem.headline: DHL Albania - it's business as usual.

text.p: Despite the impending threat of civil war, DHL Worldwide Express said in a statement it is open for business in Albania, and has no plans to shut down.
DHL's country headquarters in Tirana and its agency offices in Durres, Fier, Korca, Shkoder and Elbasan are open and are doing their best given the political uncertainty in the country.

The only area of the country where DHL can no longer operate is immediately around the Southern port city of Viore. The port used to be served by a line-haul service from the Fier agency office, but this can no longer get through.

"We are doing what we can for our customers", said DHL Albania's sales and customer service supervisor Aitan Bozo. "Tirana is under curfew from 5PM onwards, meaning that our latest cut-off time is now 3.00PM or 5.00PM in very special circumstances.

Obviously making deliveries to the rest of the country can be a little bit difficult, so we are asking customers outside Tirana to be patient and accept that there might be a delay of up to 24 hours for them.
No DHL employees have bean in any personal danger, although the situation is "very uncertain. Nobody knows what will happen tomorrow or the next day," Bozo said.
Tirana airport is at present still operating as normal. DHL currently uses Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Lufthansa flights for its consignments.
Through its Tirana office, DHL is the only air express company which operates a wholly-owned subsidiary in Albania, In Albania, DHL is adopting the same policy as in the 1991-1995 Yugoslav conflict.
The company will continue to serve customers for as long as it is physically and politically possible, and as long as its 13 employees in Albania can continue to carry out their jobs safely.

DHL in Albania started operating through an agency agreement in 1991, and opened up its own office in 1993. Its customers are evenly divided between Albanian and Western companies. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
